thread:
julia-cs: Heads-up — FairCart (enterprise) is seeing sustained 429s and occasional 504s on their Dedicated pool during marketing surge. Customer says requests queue for ~20–30s before getting 429. Zendesk ticket #FC-9876.
keith: What does infra look like? min_replicas? any quota errors?
miguel: Their Dedicated config: min_replicas=2, max_replicas=12, burst=true. Autoscaler logs show slow provisioning: provisioner took ~70s before nodes became Ready.
sara-ml: Is this cold-start of the GPU workers (model load) or just node spin-up?
miguel: Both. Node provisioning + model weights load adds up. Example log snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T09:41:12Z] autoscaler: scale request target=6 current=2 reason=queue_burst
[2026-03-15T09:41:20Z] cloud-provisioner: requested 4 g4dn nodes (req id=abc123)
[2026-03-15T09:42:34Z] cloud-provisioner: nodes ready=2 of 4
[2026-03-15T09:42:50Z] runtime: loading model redwood-13b-8bit into node node-07 (estimated 18s)
[2026-03-15T09:43:15Z] runtime: kv-cache miss warmup in progress
[2026-03-15T09:43:40Z] request-router: returning 429 queue_full after 30s
```
keith: Ouch. So autoscaler reacts but cloud provisioning + model load causes customer-visible gap. Any short-term mitigations?
julia-cs: Customer wants a fix ASAP — they hit checkout failures. SLA risk.
miguel: Quick workaround: bump min_replicas to 4 for their pool and enable pre-warm images so model loads on node init. That would reduce spin-up time. We can do this per-customer config.
sara-ml: Also can we enable fast-start caching for hottest prompts (prefix cache)? Might help while nodes boot.
ops-bot: autoscaler: attempted scale +4 -> new_target=6 (id=scale-1807659999) status=initiated :rocket:
deploy-bot: rolling config patch to dedicated-config/faircart: {"min_replicas":4} triggered by miguel — staged to prod pool fc-pool-1
keith: I'll approve the temp bump. But we need a permanent fix: suggestions?
miguel: Medium-term: keep a small warm standby (min_replicas tuned by traffic percentiles) and implement async model prefetch on node creation so model load overlaps with instance warmup. Also we should consider reducing model load time via sharded checkpoint lazy-load.
sara-ml: We should add a runbook: when a customer reports queueing/429 during surge, check: 1) min_replicas, 2) cloud quotas (concurrent instance caps), 3) recent deploys that might evict images, 4) model size and quantization.
julia-cs: Repro steps I used to validate locally (shared with customer):
```
# reproduce with k6 load targeting fc-pool-1
k6 run --vus 300 --duration 2m surge.js --out json=out.json
# check autoscaler events
kubectl -n dedicated logs deploy/autoscaler --tail=200
```
keith: Any quota or API error we should be aware of?
miguel: Not from cloud side in this incident — just cold provisioning latency. But we saw occasional 403s during burst window for their customer token; that was transient and due to rate-limited auth backend (resolved).
julia-cs: Customer updated ticket: implemented the min_replicas=4 change and saw 90% drop in 429s on the next surge. They thanked us but want a formal timeline for a permanent mitigation.
keith: Action items:
- miguel: implement async model prefetch prototype + estimate (ETA 2w)
- eng-runtime (sara-ml): prototype lazy-shard load to cut model init by ~40% (ETA 3w)
- devops: add per-customer pre-warm flag and expose in Console (ETA 1w)
- customer-success (julia-cs): confirm with FairCart the temporary config & update SLA notes (today)
Please add to the oncall rota if anything spikes tonight.
deploy-bot: config patch applied to fc-pool-1 (change set cs-1807660001) :white_check_mark:
miguel: I'll follow up with telemetry snapshots (cpu, queue_length, provision_latency) and attach to the Zendesk ticket.
julia-cs: Thanks all — closing the immediate escalation. Will re-open if customer reports recurrence. :thumbsup:
